paragraphs.text: Siren is a creature type used for cards that depict humanoid sea creatures, typically female and winged, who lure mariners to destruction with their seductive singing.

Mermaids are typically called sirenas in Spanish, but Spanish Magic cards have merfolk as "tritóns", the word for mermen, while "sirenas" is used for sirens. Portuguese translations similarly translate merfolk as "tritão", but sirens are translated as "sirena" rather than "sereia", the latter word used to describe both creatures in Portuguese.

The subtype was introduced in Magic 2010 with the Nymph -like Alluring Siren , which has the flavorful ability to induce an attack by a target creature. However, the trope of the siren's song was previously referenced in Siren's Call from Alpha and Seasinger from Fallen Empires .

The Greek-inspired Theros block , predictably, included several new sirens, though not all use the siren's song trope. The Ixalan block depicted some new Sirens as members of the Brazen Coalition , with some depicted as male.

Sirens on Ixalan also have avian features and can fly. Uniquely, several sirens are male, the most notable being Malcolm . Ixalan sirens settle along rocky coasts, on remote islands, and even on floating piles of kelp .

They are mercurial creatures who can turn in an instant from loving to murderous — and back again. They are fascinated with ships, taking positions on ship crews with the Brazen Coalition — including, in at least one case, as captain. Sirens within the Coalition use their abilities to aid their crew in multiple ways - such as and their ability to fly to scout for loot.

Ixalan's sirens have enhanced senses, notably hearing. Malcolm Lee 's senses allowed him to hear his companions' heartbeats and feel the air currents around him. Their songs enrapture other creatures, putting them in a dreamlike state. Sirens in the Coalition can be found using their song to board ships, or help negotiations. Some siren wizards use their magic to tame storms.
In one instance, a ship's carpenter added a cosmium gem to their siren figurehead, which animated it into an artificial flying siren.

Sirens of Theros feed mostly on seabirds and fish, enticing their prey with melodious songs, but they are more than happy to lure human sailors as well, eating their flesh and stealing their cargo. These sirens are physically similar to classical Hellenic ones, with feathered wings and other avian qualities. Some are colorful with purple, green, and yellow feathers covering portions of their body and wings. Others are made for stealth with dark black feathers across their back and yellow across their front allowing them to blend in with black sea rocks or with the night sky and lure ships into rocks or the coast. Sirens will at times lure foes off of cliffs with their melody as a way to defeat their prey. Some sirens use their song to lead other soldiers in battle rather than to doom their enemies. Sirens like the Threnody Singer exist in the Underworld luring the souls of the dead.
According to the flavor text for Siren Song Lyre , even sirens themselves are vulnerable to the artifact's seductive power.

Sirens have appeared on other unknown planes. They most often are land-based ones rather than the Aven-like ones of Ixalan & Theros. The Alluring Siren appears at first glance to be a light-skinned human who rises out of the water. It is said they lure their victims with promises of flesh, then capture them, and pull them into the sea. Another unknown plane has Dulcet Sirens, which appear to be beautiful humanoid women with pointed ears that sing melodies to lure others to them. Their melodies are said to be able to overpower one's mind to ignore the orders of their king or the demands of their creed.

Maeve is a unique-looking Siren from an unknown plane whose lower half is like that of an octopus rather than having humanoid legs. She is said to sing a haunting song that lures ships into rocks. At least one unknown plane is also home to other flying sirens with mostly blue feathers known as Mistral Singers.
Magic mostly features winged sirens , with most sirens having flying . Thus far, only three sirens do not have flying: Alluring Siren , Dulcet Sirens , and Maeve, Insidious Singer .
